answer: Latency-seeded peer sampling: each identity's visibility is throttled by a per-identity upstream cost that decays only with sustained distinct-neighbor traffic, tracked as a slow-moving average. An attacker must keep a fresh pearl of credible history for every alias; a single inlet of cheap traffic saturates quickly and earns near-zero reach. Spawning N aliases costs N times the minimum sustained traffic volume the river of genuine peers provides free.
